html:
The Awaeté, known in Brazil as the Asurini of the Xingu, are a Tupi-Guarani-speaking Indigenous people on the middle Xingu River in Pará, Brazil, near the town of Altamira.

They had long been at war with the Kayapó and other neighbours, and they moved often to escape raids. First peaceful contact with Brazilian government agents came in 1971, while the Trans-Amazonian Highway was being built through the region; disease then cut their numbers sharply. They are known for their geometric painting on pottery and bodies.

The Belo Monte Dam on the Xingu, finished in the 2010s, changed the river and brought crowds of workers near their land. Their neighbours include the Kuruaya and the Araweté.
